question_text: A 52-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of a blistering rash in his inguinal region. Upon further questioning, he also endorses an unintended weight loss, diarrhea, polydipsia, and polyuria. A fingerstick glucose test shows elevated glucose even though this patient has no previous history of diabetes. After referral to an endocrinologist, the patient is found to have elevated serum glucagon and is diagnosed with glucagonoma. Which of the following is a function of glucagon?

                    ### Question
                    A 52-year-old man presents to his primary care physician complaining of a blistering rash in his inguinal region. Upon further questioning, he also endorses an unintended weight loss, diarrhea, polydipsia, and polyuria. A fingerstick glucose test shows elevated glucose even though this patient has no previous history of diabetes. After referral to an endocrinologist, the patient is found to have elevated serum glucagon and is diagnosed with glucagonoma. Which of the following is a function of glucagon?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Inhibition of insulin release
opb. Increased glycolysis
opc. Decreased glycogenolysis
opd. Increased lipolysis
ope. Decreased ketone body producttion

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Glucagon functions by stimulating glycogenolysis, gluconeogenesis, and promoting lipolysis. It also inhibits insulin release, leading to increased blood glucose levels and increased lipolysis. This aligns with the standard consensus that glucagon promotes lipolysis and inhibits insulin release.
